verdict.justification: A is the stronger foundational workflow because it defines gate ownership, approval requirements, outputs, and exception handling more completely. Both correctly resolve the conflicting price-change instructions in favor of the governing r2 record and explicitly label the workflow as an unapproved recommendation. A adds enforceable controls—“a gate closes only when all listed approvers sign digitally” and ERP “price updates only after approval”—whereas B introduces “G3: Commercial clearance” without specifying its approvers or clearance criteria. A also handles no-cost changes more rigorously by requiring supplier confirmation of a zero delta and reclassification if a price claim follows; B relies on recording and notification at that point. Its platform blueprint is more implementation-ready, with explicit core data objects, approval delegation, integration controls, and an automatically compiled approval file. A is considerably denser and less well suited to the requested 2–3-page executive format, but its stronger governance and operational specificity outweigh that presentation disadvantage.

decisive_issues.issue: The commercial-clearance gate lacks a defined approval layer or decision criteria.
The no-cost change route does not explicitly require supplier confirmation of zero commercial impact.
decisive_issues.quote: Recorded and notified to all functions; no re-quote

decisive_issues.issue: Explicit gate-completion, rejection, and unsigned-version controls make the proposed workflow more executable.
decisive_issues.quote: a gate closes only when all listed approvers sign digitally; a rejection returns the item to the previous step with mandatory comments; no step after a gate can start on an unsigned version

decisive_issues.issue: The platform requirements explicitly prevent unapproved price changes from reaching ERP.
decisive_issues.quote: ERP (supplier master, price updates only after approval)
